text.p: British floor-coverings retailer Carpetright Plc, which reports annual results next Tuesday, needs to reassure investors on growth and its chances for sharing in a predicted spending spree on household durables, retail analysts said on Friday.

Confidence in the retailer, which is forecast to boost annual profits by about 29 percent, has taken a hammering since January after chairman and chief executive Lord Harris sold four million of his shares.
The stock has come down from a high this year of more than 600 pence to stand at 446 pence at 0804 GMT on Friday.

Concern that the carpet market has been sluggish coupled with worries Carpetright's rapid growth rate might be tailing off, have depressed the shares and earnings forecasts, retail analysts said. Harris's share sale further undermined sentiment, they said.
"When he sold, that put the skids under the share price," said one retail analyst.
Analysts believe the carpet trade was very poor in the run up to Britain's general election on May 1, as consumers put off making purchases.
But there are hopes some of the cash flooding into peoples' pockets from the demutualisation of mortgage lenders and insurers, may be spent on household durables such as carpets.
Further consolidation in the carpet business could also provide scope for a rebound, analysts said.
Carpetright and rival Allied Carpets Plc have become the market leaders and between them already have around a quarter of the carpet market, according the estimates from retail consultants Verdict.

The firm is forecast to make pre-tax profits of between 30.5 and 34 million stg, up from 25.2 million in the year to end April 1996. Analysts expect a dividend of about 19 pence a share, against 14.5 pence last time.
